strategy.action_description: Retile only the GEMM2 FP4 dequant inner loop so each stage2 thread computes a small adjacent hidden-column microtile, preferably two H columns, for the same active expert slot. Load each mid activation block once, load the two packed FP4 weight rows and scale rows with the existing cache-policy helpers, maintain two FP32 accumulators, and write/reduce the two outputs independently through the parent finalize path. Keep scheduling, GEMM1, and T/top-k semantics unchanged.
strategy.evidence_chain: The current GEMM2 helper reloads the same mid row for every hidden column h, while H=4096 and I=1024 make mid activation bandwidth/cache reuse important. Prior tiled-dequant attempts focused on GEMM1 shared-hidden tiling and slowed down; this is a different GEMM2 output-column microtile that reuses activations across adjacent output rows without changing the grouped schedule. The existing helper already vectorizes FP4 weights and scales, so the new lever is activation reuse versus register pressure.
strategy.expected_impact: May reduce repeated mid activation loads in GEMM2 and improve arithmetic intensity for the down projection, while preserving the proven warp-sliced GEMM1 path.
strategy.risks: Two-column accumulation increases registers and may reduce occupancy. Adjacent H rows have separate FP4 weights/scales, so the implementation must avoid assuming contiguous scale layout beyond the documented [expert, H, scale_col] row-major shape.
